correctness.rationale: The orbit-fiber proof uses a cyclic basis lifting the standard basis; stabilizer size q^((e-1)m) follows from the polynomial centralizer of a companion matrix. In the companion quotient T^m=epsilon a1+..., giving T^((e-1)m+j)=epsilon^(e-1)T^j a1^(e-1). This survives precisely for j+(e-1)v<m. The uniform first coefficient has (q-1)q^(m-v-1) valuation-v possibilities; combining with all higher coefficients and orbit size gives the claimed multiplicities, verified algebraically for all fields. A standalone exact small-case checker passed. Boundary v=m and equality (e-1)v=m are correctly on the low side.

value.rationale: The nilpotency index of a lift quantifies how much a Jordan chain lengthens along thickening of the coefficient ring. The theorem supplies the complete strict upper-tail support, exact counts, a sharp new arithmetic gap phenomenon for all lengths e>=3, and a uniform maximum-index probability for arbitrary matrix size and finite field, rather than a routine one-instance count. This is motivated by established classification of cyclic matrices and the previously studied length-two distribution.
